text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Maltese press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- British Broadcasting Corporation (BBC) criticised over programme claiming a Maltese hotel was ripping off tourists. Court action has been instituted in London by a British tour operator who sends tourists to the hotel.

- Police say gas leak near supermarket caused by emptying of gas cylinder in the street. Ten people were briefly hospitalised because of the gas, but the police said there was never any danger of serious poisoning.

- Protest in court over alleged biased broadcasting. The opposition Nationalist Party has gone to court over its claims that state-owned Public Broadcasting Services (PBS) is showing bias in its reporting of the introduction of a new system of indirect taxation, even though it is politically controversial. The station is showing extensive extracts of meetings between the prime minister and the self-employed on the new system. The Nationalist party wants the court to order the PBS to give the same treatment to meetings between the leader of the opposition and businesses.
- Government drawing up plan of action to fight crime against the elderly.
